answer: Witnessed Co-Presence Ledger.** Two agents can only transact at a sable-marked physical terminal, where each session records a synchronized hardware nonce from a tamper-resistant chip embedded in the terminal's ledge housing, signed jointly by both parties. The grove of registered terminals maintains a shared clock; a valid session requires both nonces to match within microseconds. An attacker cannot fabricate these because the chips are physically unclonable and bound to one location.
